commentary.text: I’m claiming a central square immediately, building toward center occupation while keeping Red’s other pieces available as future sandwich anchors.
I’m contesting the center immediately, denying Red–Yellow an easy occupation path while establishing Blue on a key central square.

I’m taking a second central square with Yellow. This supports the center-occupation plan and creates a useful Yellow sandwich: if Green enters (4,3), Yellow can later land on (4,2) with (4,4) as the far anchor.
I’m taking a central square immediately, building a Blue–Green foothold while restricting Yellow’s options around the center.
I’m exploiting the same-color Red anchor at (3,3): landing at (3,5) sandwiches and captures Blue on (3,4), removing an opponent from the center while preserving our two occupied central squares.
I’m developing Blue toward the open central square at (3,4). The piece is safe at (2,4) and can contest the center vertically on a later Blue turn.

I’m using Yellow’s anchor at (4,4): moving the piece from (7,2) to (4,2) sandwiches and captures Green at (4,3), clearing a third central square for our center-occupation plan while inflicting Green’s first loss.
I’m advancing Green beside the center, pressuring Red’s central piece while preserving routes for a later center occupation.

I’m using Red’s center anchor at (3,3) to sandwich Green on (3,2), bringing Green to two losses and preserving our central foothold. This also places Red at (3,1) as a useful horizontal anchor while we look for an elimination or a safe route to complete the center.
I’m taking a central square immediately, building toward the four-square occupation win while splitting Red’s pieces on row 3.

I’m occupying the third central square, leaving Blue’s piece at (3,4) as the only obstacle to an immediate center victory. This creates sustained pressure: if Blue vacates that square, either Red or Yellow may be able to complete the center, while our existing Red flanks continue to constrain it.
I’m placing Green above the central column, creating a strong future sandwich threat through (4,3) and (3,3) while contesting the center.

I’m temporarily lifting the Red flank from (3,5) to create a forced center dilemma. If Blue vacates (3,4), Yellow can occupy it for immediate center victory; if Blue remains, Red can return to (3,5) next turn and re-trigger the sandwich with Red at (3,3).
I’m using the central Blue piece as the far flank to capture Yellow on (4,4), weakening their center presence while keeping Blue’s own central foothold intact.
I’m exploiting the vertical Green flank: landing at (5,3) sandwiches the Yellow and Red pieces above it against Green at (2,3), clearing two central squares and advancing both enemy loss counts.

I’m restoring Red’s flank at (3,5), threatening to land the Red piece from (3,1) on (3,3) and sandwich Blue at (3,4). This pressures Blue to abandon the center; if it stays, we can inflict Blue’s second loss.

I’m withdrawing the exposed Blue piece from Red’s horizontal pincer while retaining a foothold in the center. The move also consolidates with the Blue piece below and advances the center-occupation plan.

I’m shifting Yellow onto column 2 to reopen the route toward (4,2), avoiding exposed placements beside Blue’s anchors. From there, Yellow can approach the vacant central square (4,3) or establish a same-color flank against the Blue piece at (4,4).
I’m taking the lower-left center square beside Blue’s piece, building toward a center-occupation win while keeping Green mobile and protected from any immediate capture.
I’m reoccupying (3,3) with Red while retaining the Red flank at (3,5). This rebuilds our center presence and preserves a future sandwich against any Blue piece settling on (3,4).
I’m advancing the central Blue piece to build a three-square center threat while opening (4,4) for the Blue piece behind it.

I’m aligning Yellow on column 4 so it can enter the vacant center at (4,4) next turn. This preserves the piece at (7,2) for a future flank against Green on row 4 while keeping Yellow safely away from immediate capture.

I’m vacating (2,3) while keeping the Green piece ready to return there: a later return would sandwich the Red center piece against Green at (4,3), opening the central square and advancing our center-control threat.
I’m lifting the Red flank while keeping the center anchor at (3,3). Returning to (3,5) next Red turn will re-trigger the sandwich on Blue at (3,4), forcing it to retreat or suffer a second loss.
I’m occupying the open central square, strengthening our center-control threat while preserving the Blue piece already on the upper central square.

I’m placing Yellow at (4,2) as the left anchor against the mixed Green–Blue line on row 4. A later Yellow landing on (4,5) would sandwich both pieces, so this pressures Green and Blue to break their central formation while keeping Yellow out of an immediate capture.
I’m removing Red’s central blocker with a Green sandwich. This opens (3,3), allowing Blue to occupy it next turn and complete Team B’s control of all four center squares.

I’m placing Red at (3,2) to rebuild the lost central anchor. If Blue moves into (3,3), Red can land at (3,5) and sandwich both central Blue pieces; otherwise this piece can step into (3,3) to restore our center foothold.
I preserve the three occupied center squares while repositioning the edge Blue piece. Yellow cannot prevent Green from filling (3,3) next turn to complete Team B’s center occupation.

I’m staging Yellow on column 5 to threaten (4,5), which would sandwich the Blue–Green pair on row 4 against Yellow at (4,2), eliminate Green, and put Blue one loss from elimination. This forces the central formation to break.
This fills the last unoccupied central square, joining our Blue and Green pieces to complete center occupation and win immediately.
